title.en: Volume 174 Biographies 99: Li Fengji, Yuan Zhen, Niu Sengru and Grandson: Hui, Li Zongmin, Yang Sifu
title.raw: 卷一百七十四 列傳第九十九 李逢吉 元稹 牛僧儒孫:徽 李宗閔 楊嗣復 Volume 174 Biographies 99: Li Fengji, Yuan Zhen, Niu Sengru and Grandson: Hui, Li Zongmin, Yang Sifu

sentences.zh: 李逢吉李逢吉，字虛舟，系出隴西。

translations.literal: Li Fengji—Li Fengji, styled Xuzhou, traced his lineage to Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengji, styled Xuzhou, was descended from Longxi.

sentences.zh: 父顏，有錮疾，逢吉自料醫劑，遂通方書。

translations.literal: His father Yan had a chronic ailment; Fengji himself prepared medical prescriptions and thereby mastered medical texts.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan suffered from a chronic illness; Fengji compounded medicines for him himself and in time became versed in medical treatises.

sentences.zh: 舉明經，又擢進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination and was also selected on the jinshi degree list.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Classics examination and was also selected on the jinshi roster.

sentences.zh: 范希朝表為振武掌書記，薦之德宗，拜左拾遺。

translations.literal: Fan Xichao memorialized to appoint him secretary to the Zhenwu command; he recommended him to Emperor Dezong, who invested him as Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xichao nominated him as secretary to the Zhenwu command and recommended him to Emperor Dezong, who appointed him Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 元和時，遷給事中、皇太子侍讀。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, he was transferred to Supervising Censor and Reader to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe reign, he was promoted to Supervising Censor and Reader to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 改中書舍人，知禮部貢舉。

translations.literal: He was changed to Drafting Secretary and put in charge of the Ministry of Rites examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Drafting Secretary and placed in charge of the Ministry of Rites examination.

sentences.zh: 未已事，拜門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Before he had finished the matter, he was invested as Vice Director of the Chancellery and Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had finished his duties, he was appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery and Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 詔禮部尚書王播署榜。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Minister of Rites Wang Bo to post the examination roster.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed Minister of Rites Wang Bo to publish the examination results.

sentences.zh: 逢吉性忌刻，險譎多端。

translations.literal: Fengji was jealous and harsh by nature, treacherous and full of schemes.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Fengji was jealous and vindictive, treacherous and endlessly scheming.

sentences.zh: 及得位，務償好惡。

translations.literal: Once he gained office, he strove to settle scores of likes and dislikes.
translations.idiomatic: Once in power, he set about settling old scores.

sentences.zh: 裴度討淮西，逢吉慮成功，密圖沮止，趣和議者請罷諸道兵。

translations.literal: When Pei Du campaigned against Huaixi, Fengji feared success and secretly plotted to obstruct it, urging those favoring peace talks to request withdrawal of all provincial armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du campaigned against Huaixi, Fengji feared he would succeed and secretly plotted to thwart him, pressing those who favored peace to demand that all provincial armies be withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 憲宗知而惡之，出為劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong learned of this and despised him, sending him out as military governor of Jiannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong learned of this and came to despise him, dispatching him as military governor of Jiannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，徙山南東道。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne, Fengji was transferred to Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, he was transferred to Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 緣講侍恩，陰結近幸。

translations.literal: Relying on his role as tutor to cultivate favor, he secretly allied with close favorites.
translations.idiomatic: Exploiting his position as tutor to cultivate imperial favor, he secretly cultivated ties with the emperor's close favorites.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年，召入為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changqing, he was recalled and made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changqing, he was recalled to serve as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 時度與元稹知政，度嘗條稹憸佞，逢吉以為其隙易乘，遂並中之，遣人上變，言：「和王傅于方結客，欲為稹刺度。」

translations.literal: At the time Pei Du and Yuan Zhen held power; Du had once listed Zhen's crafty sycophancy, and Fengji thought the rift easy to exploit, so he struck at both together, sending someone to report an emergency, saying: "Royal Tutor Yu Fang has gathered clients and intends to have Zhen assassinate Du."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Pei Du and Yuan Zhen shared power; Du had once catalogued Zhen's sly flattery, and Fengji saw an opening easy to exploit, so he attacked them both at once, sending someone to lodge an emergency report, saying: "Royal Tutor Yu Fang has gathered followers and intends to have Zhen assassinate Du."

sentences.zh: 帝命尚書左僕射韓皋、給事中鄭覃與逢吉參鞠方，無狀，稹、度坐是皆罷，逢吉代為門下侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Left Vice Director Han Gao, Supervising Censor Zheng Tan, and Fengji jointly to examine Fang; they found no substance to the charge, but both Zhen and Du were dismissed as a result, and Fengji replaced Du as Vice Director of the Chancellery and Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Left Vice Director Han Gao, Supervising Censor Zheng Tan, and Fengji to examine Fang jointly; they found no basis for the accusation, yet both Zhen and Du were dismissed on that account, and Fengji replaced Du as Vice Director of the Chancellery and Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 因以恩爵動詭薄者，更相挺以詆傷度，於是李紳、韋處厚等誦言度為逢吉排迮，度初得留。

translations.literal: Thereupon, mobilizing those he had favored with titles and positions, he had them in turn support one another to slander Du; then Li Shen, Wei Chuhou, and others proclaimed that Du was being squeezed out by Fengji, and Du was initially allowed to remain.
translations.idiomatic: He then rallied those he had favored with titles and rewards, and they took turns bolstering one another to attack Du; Li Shen, Wei Chuhou, and others publicly declared that Du was being driven out by Fengji, and Du was at first permitted to stay.

sentences.zh: 時已失河朔，王智興以徐叛，李騕以汴叛，國威不振，天下延頸俟相度，而中外交章言之，帝訖不省，度遂外遷。

translations.literal: By then the empire had lost Hebei; Wang Zhixing rebelled at Xu and Li Jiao at Bian; national prestige was shaken; all under heaven craned their necks awaiting Du as chancellor, and memorials from court and frontier alike urged it, yet the Emperor never took heed, and Du was eventually transferred outward.
translations.idiomatic: By then the empire had lost control of Hebei; Wang Zhixing rebelled at Xu and Li Jiao at Bian; the nation's prestige was shattered, and all under heaven waited eagerly for Du to become chancellor, with memorials from court and frontier alike urging it—but the Emperor never took heed, and Du was eventually sent away from the capital.

sentences.zh: 騕平，進尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: When Jiao was suppressed, Fengji was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiao's rebellion was put down, he was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝暴疾，中外阻遏，逢吉因中人梁守謙、劉弘規、王守澄議，請立景王為皇太子，帝不能言，頷之而已。

translations.literal: The Emperor fell gravely ill and communication between court and outside was blocked; Fengji, consulting with eunuchs Liang Shouqian, Liu Honggui, and Wang Shoucheng, proposed installing Prince Jing as crown prince; the Emperor could not speak but nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor fell gravely ill and communication between court and outside was cut off, Fengji consulted with the eunuchs Liang Shouqian, Liu Honggui, and Wang Shoucheng and proposed that Prince Jing be made crown prince; the Emperor could not speak but nodded his assent.

sentences.zh: 明日下詔，皇太子遂定。

translations.literal: The next day an edict was issued and the crown prince was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict was promulgated and the succession was settled.

sentences.zh: 鄭注得幸于王守澄，逢吉遣從子訓賂注，結守澄為奧援，自是肆志無所憚。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhu won Wang Shoucheng's favor; Fengji sent his nephew Xun to bribe Zhu and allied with Shoucheng as a hidden support, after which he indulged his will without fear.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhu won the favor of Wang Shoucheng; Fengji sent his nephew Xun to bribe Zhu and secured Shoucheng as a hidden patron, after which he indulged his will without restraint.

sentences.zh: 其党有張又新、李續、張權輿、劉棲楚、李虞、程昔范、薑洽及訓八人，而傅會者又八人，皆任要劇，故號「八關十六子」。

translations.literal: His faction included Zhang Youxin, Li Xu, Zhang Quanyu, Liu Qichu, Li Yu, Cheng Xifan, Jiang Qia, and Xun—eight men—and eight more who attached themselves to them, all holding weighty posts, hence they were called the "Eight Passes and Sixteen Sons."
translations.idiomatic: His faction numbered Zhang Youxin, Li Xu, Zhang Quanyu, Liu Qichu, Li Yu, Cheng Xifan, Jiang Qia, and Xun—eight men—with eight more who attached themselves to them, all holding important posts; they were therefore called the "Eight Passes and Sixteen Sons."

sentences.zh: 有所求請，先賂關子，後達于逢吉，無不得所欲。

translations.literal: Anyone with a request would first bribe a "Pass" member, then reach Fengji, and obtain whatever they desired.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone seeking a favor would first bribe one of the "Passes," then reach Fengji, and obtain whatever he wished.

sentences.zh: 未幾，封涼國公。

translations.literal: Before long he was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 敬宗新立，度求入覲，逢吉不自安，張權輿為作讖言以沮度，而韋處厚亟為帝言之，計卒不行。

translations.literal: When the new Emperor Jingzong took the throne, Du sought to return for an audience; Fengji was uneasy, and Zhang Quanyu composed a prophecy to deter him, but Wei Chuhou repeatedly pleaded with the Emperor on Du's behalf, and the plan ultimately failed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingzong had just ascended the throne, Du sought to return to court; Fengji was ill at ease, and Zhang Quanyu fabricated a prophecy to block him, but Wei Chuhou repeatedly urged the Emperor on Du's behalf, and the scheme ultimately failed.

sentences.zh: 有武昭者，陳留人，果敢而辯。

translations.literal: There was a Wu Zhao, a man of Chenliu, bold and eloquent.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Wu Zhao, a native of Chenliu, bold and eloquent.

sentences.zh: 度之討蔡，遣說吳元濟，元濟臨以兵，辭不撓，厚禮遣還，度署以軍職，從鎮太原，除石州刺史。

translations.literal: When Du campaigned against Cai, he sent Zhao to persuade Wu Yuanji; Yuanji confronted him with troops, but Zhao's words did not waver; Yuanji treated him generously and sent him back; Du gave him a military post and kept him at Taiyuan, later appointing him prefect of Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Du campaigned against Cai, he sent Zhao to persuade Wu Yuanji; Yuanji confronted him with troops, but Zhao's words did not falter; Yuanji treated him generously and sent him back; Du gave him a military appointment and kept him at Taiyuan, later making him prefect of Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 罷歸不得用，怨望，與太學博士李涉、金吾兵曹參軍茅匯居長安中，以氣俠相許。

translations.literal: Dismissed and sent home without further appointment, Zhao nursed resentment; he lived in Chang'an with Imperial Academy Erudite Li She and Jinwu Army Staff Officer Mao Hui, bound together by bravado and chivalry.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed and sent home without further appointment, he nursed resentment; he lived in Chang'an with Imperial Academy Erudite Li She and Jinwu Army Staff Officer Mao Hui, bound to one another by bravado and chivalry.

sentences.zh: 逢吉與李程同執政，不葉。

translations.literal: Fengji and Li Cheng held power together but did not get along.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji and Li Cheng shared power but did not get along.

sentences.zh: 程族人仍叔謂昭曰：「丞相欲用君，顧逢吉持不可。」

translations.literal: Cheng's clansman Reishu told Zhao: "The Chancellor wishes to employ you, but Fengji alone opposes it."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's clansman Reishu told Zhao: "The Chancellor wishes to employ you, but Fengji alone stands in the way."

sentences.zh: 昭愈憤，酒所，語其友劉審，欲刺逢吉。

translations.literal: Zhao grew angrier; while drunk he told his friend Liu Shen he wanted to assassinate Fengji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao grew still angrier; while drunk he told his friend Liu Shen that he wanted to assassinate Fengji.

sentences.zh: 審竊語權輿，逢吉因匯召見昭，厚相結納，忿隙得解。

translations.literal: Shen secretly informed Quanyu; Fengji then had Hui summon Zhao, treated him generously and won him over, and the feud was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Shen secretly told Quanyu; Fengji then had Hui summon Zhao, treated him generously and won him over, and the feud was resolved.

sentences.zh: 逢吉素厚待匯，嘗與書曰：「足下當以'自求'字僕，吾當以'利見'字君。」

translations.literal: Fengji had always treated Hui well and once wrote to him: "You ought to style me with the characters for 'self-seeking'; I ought to style you with the characters for 'profit in sight."
translations.idiomatic: Fengji had always treated Hui generously and once wrote to him: "You ought to style me with the characters for 'self-seeking'; I ought to style you with the characters for 'profit in sight."

sentences.zh: 辭頗猥昵。

translations.literal: The wording was quite vulgar and intimate.
translations.idiomatic: The language was quite vulgar and familiar.

sentences.zh: 及度將還，復命人發昭事。

translations.literal: When Du was about to return, Fengji again had someone expose Zhao's affair.
translations.idiomatic: When Du was about to return to court, Fengji again had someone expose Zhao's affair.

sentences.zh: 由是昭、匯皆下獄，命御史中丞王播按之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhao and Hui were both imprisoned, and the Emperor ordered Investigation Commissioner Wang Bo to examine the case.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Zhao and Hui were both imprisoned, and the Emperor ordered Investigation Commissioner Wang Bo to investigate.

sentences.zh: 訓諷匯使誣昭與李程同謀，不然且死。

translations.literal: Xun urged Hui to falsely implicate Zhao together with Li Cheng, or face death.
translations.idiomatic: Xun pressured Hui to falsely implicate Zhao in a plot with Li Cheng, threatening death if he refused.

sentences.zh: 匯不可，曰：「誣人以自免，不為也！」

translations.literal: Hui refused, saying: "To frame another to save oneself—I will not do it!"
translations.idiomatic: Hui refused, saying: "To frame another to save myself—I will not do it!"

sentences.zh: 獄成，昭榜死，匯流崖州，涉康州，仍叔貶道州司馬，訓流象州。

translations.literal: When the case was concluded, Zhao was executed by beating, Hui was banished to Yazhou, She to Kangzhou, Reishu demoted to Prefectural Militia Vice Commandant of Daozhou, and Xun exiled to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was concluded, Zhao was beaten to death, Hui was banished to Yazhou, She to Kangzhou, Reishu was demoted to Prefectural Militia Vice Commandant of Daozhou, and Xun was exiled to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 擢審長壽主簿。

translations.literal: Shen was promoted to Recorder of Changshou.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was promoted to Recorder of Changshou.

sentences.zh: 而逢吉謀益露。

translations.literal: Fengji's scheming thus became still more exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji's scheming thus became still more exposed.

sentences.zh: 昭死，人皆冤之。

translations.literal: When Zhao died, everyone considered it a miscarriage of justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao died, everyone considered it a miscarriage of justice.

sentences.zh: 初，逢吉興昭獄以止度入而不果，天子知度忠，卒相之。

translations.literal: Initially Fengji had engineered the Zhao case to prevent Du's return but failed; the Son of Heaven knew Du was loyal and ultimately made him chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: At first Fengji had engineered the Zhao case to keep Du from returning to court, but failed; the Son of Heaven knew Du was loyal and ultimately made him chancellor.

sentences.zh: 逢吉於是浸疏，以檢校司空、平章事為山南東道節度使，表李續自副，張又新行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Fengji was then gradually estranged and sent out as Honorary Grand Guardian and Director of the Chancellery serving as military governor of Shannan East Circuit; he memorialized to have Li Xu as his deputy and Zhang Youxin as staff army vice commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji was then gradually estranged and sent out as Honorary Grand Guardian and Director of the Chancellery serving as military governor of Shannan East Circuit; he memorialized to have Li Xu as his deputy and Zhang Youxin as staff army vice commandant.

sentences.zh: 頃之，檢校司徒。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Honorary Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Honorary Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 初，門下史田伾倚逢吉親信，顧財利，進婢，嬖之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Gate Clerk Tian Zhen had relied on Fengji's trust and sought profit; he presented a maid servant whom Fengji favored.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Gate Clerk Tian Zhen had relied on Fengji's trust and sought profit; he presented a maid servant whom Fengji took as a favorite.

sentences.zh: 伾坐事匿逢吉家，名捕弗獲。

translations.literal: When Zhen was implicated in a case he hid in Fengji's house, and though officially sought he could not be found.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen was implicated in a case he hid in Fengji's house, and though officially sought he could not be found.

sentences.zh: 及出鎮，表隨軍，滿歲不敢集，使人偽過門下省，調房州司馬。

translations.literal: When Fengji went out to his command, he had Zhen follow the army; for a full year Zhen dared not assemble, and had someone falsely pass through the Gate Department to obtain appointment as Prefectural Militia Vice Commandant of Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Fengji went out to his command, he had Zhen follow the army; for a full year Zhen dared not report for duty, and had someone falsely pass through the Gate Department to obtain appointment as Prefectural Militia Vice Commandant of Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 為有司所發，即襄州捕之，詭讕不遣。

translations.literal: Exposed by the relevant office, he was immediately arrested at Xiangzhou, but Fengji prevaricated and would not send him.
translations.idiomatic: Exposed by the relevant office, he was immediately arrested at Xiangzhou, but Fengji prevaricated and would not surrender him.

sentences.zh: 御史劾奏，詔奪一季俸，因是貶續為涪州刺史，又新汀州刺史。

translations.literal: The censor memorialized an impeachment; the Emperor ordered one season's salary forfeited, and Li Xu was demoted to Prefect of Fu and Youxin to Prefect of Ting.
translations.idiomatic: The censor memorialized an impeachment; the Emperor ordered one season's salary forfeited, and Li Xu was demoted to Prefect of Fu and Youxin to Prefect of Ting.

sentences.zh: 久乃徙宣武，以太子太師為東都留守。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Xuanwu, and then served as Eastern Capital Intendant with the title Grand Preceptor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was transferred to Xuanwu, and then served as Eastern Capital Intendant with the title Grand Preceptor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 及訓用事，召拜尚書左僕射，足病不能朝，以司徒致仕。

translations.literal: When Xun came to power, Fengji was summoned and appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; afflicted with foot ailment he could not attend court and retired with the title Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun came to power, he was summoned and appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; afflicted with a foot ailment he could not attend court and retired with the title Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十八，贈太尉，諡曰成。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-eight, posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Marshal and given the posthumous name Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-eight, posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Marshal and given the posthumous name Cheng.

sentences.zh: 無子，以從弟子植嗣。

translations.literal: He had no son and had his nephew Zhi succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son and had his nephew Zhi succeed him.

sentences.zh: 元稹元稹，字微之，河南河南人。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhen—Yuan Zhen, styled Weizhi, was a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen, styled Weizhi, was a native of Henan.

sentences.zh: 六代祖岩，為隋兵部尚書。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Yan had been Minister of War under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Yan had served as Minister of War under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 稹幼孤，母鄭賢而文，親授書傳。

translations.literal: Zhen lost his father young; his mother Zheng was talented and learned and personally taught him the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen lost his father while still a child; his mother Zheng was talented and learned and personally taught him the classics.

sentences.zh: 九歲工屬文，十五擢明經，判入等，補校書郎。

translations.literal: At nine he was skilled at composition; at fifteen he passed the Mingjing and ranked in the top tier, and was appointed Proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he was already skilled at composition; at fifteen he passed the Classics examination with a top-tier evaluation and was appointed Proofreader.

sentences.zh: 元和元年舉制科，對策第一，拜左拾遺。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe he entered the special decree examination, ranked first in the policy response, and was appointed Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanhe he entered the special decree examination, ranked first in the policy response, and was appointed Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 性明銳，遇事輒舉。

translations.literal: He was sharp and perceptive by nature and spoke up whenever something arose.
translations.idiomatic: Sharp and perceptive by nature, he spoke up whenever something arose.

sentences.zh: 始，王叔文、王伾蒙幸太子宮而橈國政，稹謂宜選正人輔導，因獻書曰：

translations.literal: At the outset, when Wang Shuwen and Wang Pi enjoyed favor in the Crown Prince's palace and disrupted state affairs, Zhen held that upright men should be chosen to guide the prince, and submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, when Wang Shuwen and Wang Pi enjoyed favor in the Crown Prince's palace and disrupted state affairs, Zhen held that upright men should be chosen to guide the prince, and submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 伏見陛下降明詔，脩廢學，增胄子，然而事有先於此，臣敢昧死言之。

translations.literal: I have observed Your Majesty's bright edict restoring abandoned studies and increasing imperial students; yet there is something that should come before this, and I dare speak at the risk of death.
translations.idiomatic: I have observed Your Majesty's enlightened edict restoring abandoned studies and increasing the number of imperial students; yet there is something that should come before this, and I dare speak even at the risk of my life.

sentences.zh: 賈誼有言：「三代之君仁且久者，教之然也。」

translations.literal: Jia Yi said: "The reason the rulers of the Three Dynasties were benevolent and long-reigning was teaching."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi said: "The reason the rulers of the Three Dynasties were benevolent and long-reigning was teaching."

sentences.zh: 周成王本中才，近管、蔡則讒入，任周、召則善聞。

translations.literal: King Cheng of Zhou was by nature of middling talent; near Guan and Cai, slander entered; with the Dukes of Zhou and Shao in charge, good counsel was heard.
translations.idiomatic: King Cheng of Zhou was by nature of middling talent; near Guan and Cai, slander entered; with the Dukes of Zhou and Shao in charge, good counsel was heard.

sentences.zh: 豈天聰明哉？

translations.literal: Was this heaven's wisdom?
translations.idiomatic: Was this heaven's wisdom?

sentences.zh: 而克終於道者，教也。

translations.literal: That he could finish the Way was due to teaching.
translations.idiomatic: That he could finish the Way was due to teaching.

sentences.zh: 始為太子也，太公為師，周公為傅，召公為保，伯禽、唐叔與游，目不閱淫豔，耳不聞優笑，居不近庸邪，玩不備珍異。

translations.literal: When he first became crown prince, the Duke of Lu was his teacher, the Duke of Zhou his aide, the Duke of Shao his guardian; Boyi and Shu of Tang kept company with him—his eyes did not behold licentious beauty, his ears did not hear comic performances, his dwelling did not approach vulgar wickedness, his pastimes did not include rare curios.
translations.idiomatic: When he first became crown prince, the Duke of Lu was his teacher, the Duke of Zhou his aide, the Duke of Shao his guardian; Boyi and Shu of Tang kept company with him—his eyes did not behold licentious beauty, his ears did not hear comic performances, his dwelling did not approach vulgar wickedness, and his pastimes did not include rare curios.

sentences.zh: 及為君也，血氣既定，游習既成，雖有放心，不能奪已成之性。

translations.literal: When he became king, his temperament was settled and his habits formed; even if wayward impulses arose, they could not overturn the character already formed.
translations.idiomatic: When he became king, his temperament was settled and his habits formed; even if wayward impulses arose, they could not overturn the character already formed.

sentences.zh: 則彼道德之言，固吾所習聞，陳之者易諭焉；

translations.literal: Then those words of virtue and the Way were what he had long been accustomed to hear—the one who set them forth was easily understood;
translations.idiomatic: Then those words of virtue and the Way were what he had long been accustomed to hear—the one who set them forth was easily understood;

sentences.zh: 回佞庸違，固吾所積懼，諂之者易辯焉。

translations.literal: Flatterers, petty men, and the refractory were what he had long accumulated fear of—the one who fawned was easily refuted.
translations.idiomatic: Flatterers, petty men, and the refractory were what he had long accumulated fear of—the one who fawned was easily refuted.

sentences.zh: 人之情莫不耀所能，黨所近，苟得志，必快其所蘊。

translations.literal: In human disposition none fail to display their talents and band with those they favor; once their ambitions are fulfilled, they must give vent to what they hold within.
translations.idiomatic: In human disposition none fail to display their talents and band with those they favor; once their ambitions are fulfilled, they must give vent to what they hold within.

sentences.zh: 物性亦然，故魚得水而遊，鳥乘風而翔，火得薪而熾。

translations.literal: The nature of things is likewise: fish swim upon gaining water, birds soar upon catching wind, fire blazes upon gaining fuel.
translations.idiomatic: The nature of things is likewise: fish swim upon gaining water, birds soar upon catching wind, fire blazes upon gaining fuel.

sentences.zh: 夫成王所蘊，道德也；

translations.literal: What King Cheng held within was virtue and the Way;
translations.idiomatic: What King Cheng held within was virtue and the Way;

sentences.zh: 所近，聖賢也。

translations.literal: Those he favored were sages and worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Those he favored were sages and worthies.

sentences.zh: 快其蘊，則興禮樂，朝諸侯，措刑罰，教之至也。

translations.literal: To give vent to what he held within was to raise ritual and music, assemble the feudal lords, set aside punishments—the utmost of teaching.
translations.idiomatic: To give vent to what he held within was to raise ritual and music, assemble the feudal lords, and set aside punishments—the utmost of teaching.

sentences.zh: 秦則不然，滅先王之學，黜師保之位。

translations.literal: Qin was not so: it extinguished the learning of the former kings and removed tutors and guardians from their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Qin was not so: it extinguished the learning of the former kings and removed tutors and guardians from their posts.

sentences.zh: 胡亥之生也，《詩》、《書》不得聞，聖賢不得近。

translations.literal: When Huhai was born, he could not hear the 《Odes》 or 《Documents》, nor draw near sages and worthies.
translations.idiomatic: When Huhai was born, he could not hear the 《Odes》 or 《Documents》, nor draw near sages and worthies.

sentences.zh: 彼趙高，刑餘之人，傅之以殘忍戕賊之術，日恣睢，天下之人未盡愚，而亥不能分馬鹿矣；

translations.literal: That Zhao Gao—a mutilated man—was made his tutor and taught him cruel, destructive methods; day by day he indulged his will, and though the people of the realm were not all stupid, Huhai could no longer tell horse from deer;
translations.idiomatic: That Zhao Gao—a mutilated man—was made his tutor and taught him cruel, destructive methods; day by day he indulged his will, and though the people of the realm were not all stupid, Huhai could no longer tell horse from deer;

sentences.zh: 高之威懾天下，而亥自幽深宮矣。

translations.literal: Gao's awe overawed all under heaven, and Huhai himself remained deep within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Gao's awe overawed all under heaven, and Huhai himself remained shut away deep within the palace.

sentences.zh: 若秦亡，則有以致之也。

translations.literal: If Qin perished, there was cause enough for it.
translations.idiomatic: If Qin perished, there was cause enough for it.

sentences.zh: 太宗為太子，選知道德者十八人與之遊；

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong was crown prince, he selected eighteen men versed in the Way and virtue to keep company with him;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong was crown prince, he selected eighteen men versed in the Way and virtue to keep company with him;

sentences.zh: 即位後，雖間宴飲食，十八人者皆在。

translations.literal: After he ascended the throne, even at occasional banquets and meals, the eighteen were all present.
translations.idiomatic: After he ascended the throne, even at occasional banquets and meals, the eighteen were all present.

sentences.zh: 上之失無不言，下之情無不達，不四三年而名高盛古，斯游習之致也。

translations.literal: The ruler's faults were all spoken of, the people's sentiments all conveyed; in less than three or four years his fame rose above antiquity—this was the effect of such companionship and habit.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler's faults were all spoken of, the people's sentiments all conveyed; in less than three or four years his fame rose above antiquity—this was the effect of such companionship and habit.

sentences.zh: 貞觀以來，保、傅皆宰相兼領，余官亦時重選，故馬周恨位高不為司議郎，其驗也。

translations.literal: Since the Zhenguan era, guardians and aides had all been concurrently held by chancellors, and the other offices were also at times carefully chosen; hence Ma Zhou regretted that high rank did not make one Remonstrance Officer—this was proof of it.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhenguan era, guardians and aides had all been concurrently held by chancellors, and the other offices were also at times carefully chosen; hence Ma Zhou regretted that high rank did not make one Remonstrance Officer—this was proof of it.

sentences.zh: 母后臨朝，剪棄王室，中、睿為太子，雖有骨鯁敢言之士，不得在調護保安職，及讒言中傷，惟樂工剖腹為證，豈不哀哉！

translations.literal: When empress dowagers held court and cut down the royal house, Zhongzong and Ruizong as crown princes—though there were blunt, outspoken men—could not hold posts of guidance and protection; when slander struck, only a musician's disembowelment served as proof—was it not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: When empress dowagers held court and cut down the royal house, Zhongzong and Ruizong as crown princes—though there were blunt, outspoken men—could not hold posts of guidance and protection; when slander struck, only a musician's disembowelment served as proof—was it not lamentable!

sentences.zh: 比來茲弊尤甚，師資保傅，不疾廢眊目貴，即休戎罷帥者處之。

translations.literal: Recently this abuse has grown especially severe: tutors, guardians, and aides are either infirm, blind, or aged nobles, or else retired generals and dismissed commanders are placed in those posts.
translations.idiomatic: Recently this abuse has grown especially severe: tutors, guardians, and aides are either infirm, blind, or aged nobles, or else retired generals and dismissed commanders are placed in those posts.

sentences.zh: 又以僻滯華首之儒備侍直、侍讀，越月逾時不得召。

translations.literal: Obscure, stagnant, white-haired scholars are also used to fill attendance and reading posts, going months and seasons without being summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Obscure, stagnant, white-haired scholars are also used to fill attendance and reading posts, going months and seasons without being summoned.

sentences.zh: 夫以匹士之愛其子，猶求明哲慈惠之師，豈天下元良而反不及乎？

translations.literal: If even a common man in loving his son still seeks a wise, clear, and kindly teacher, can the heir to all under heaven fall short of that?
translations.idiomatic: If even a common man in loving his son still seeks a wise, clear, and kindly teacher, can the heir to all under heaven fall short of that?

sentences.zh: 臣以為高祖至陛下十一聖，生而神明，長而仁聖，以是為屑屑者，故不之省。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that from Emperor Gaozu down to Your Majesty there have been eleven sage rulers, divinely gifted from birth and benevolent and sagely in maturity; because of this they regarded the matter as trivial and did not examine it.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject holds that from Emperor Gaozu down to Your Majesty there have been eleven sage rulers, divinely gifted from birth and benevolent and sagely in maturity; because of this they regarded the matter as trivial and did not examine it.

sentences.zh: 設萬世之後，有周成中才，生於深宮，無保助之教，則將不能知喜怒哀樂所自，況稼穡艱難乎！

translations.literal: Suppose ten thousand generations hence there should be a King Cheng of middling talent, born in the deep palace with no teaching from guardians and aides—then he would not even know whence joy, anger, sorrow, and delight arise, let alone the hardships of farming!
translations.idiomatic: Suppose ten thousand generations hence there should be a King Cheng of middling talent, born in the deep palace with no teaching from guardians and aides—then he would not even know whence joy, anger, sorrow, and delight arise, let alone the hardships of farming!

sentences.zh: 願令皇太子洎諸王齒胄講業，行嚴師問道之禮，輟禽色之娛，資游習之善，豈不美哉！

translations.literal: I wish that the crown prince and the princes may study at the academy and pursue their learning, observe the rites of strict teachers and inquiry into the Way, set aside entertainments of birds and beauty, and nourish the good of companionship and habit—would this not be splendid!
translations.idiomatic: I wish that the crown prince and the princes may study at the academy and pursue their learning, observe the rites of strict teachers and inquiry into the Way, set aside entertainments of birds and beauty, and nourish the good of companionship and habit—would this not be splendid!

sentences.zh: 又自以職諫諍，不得數召見，上疏曰：

translations.literal: Again, considering his office of remonstrance and that he could not often be summoned for audience, he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Again, considering his office of remonstrance and that he could not often be summoned for audience, he submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞治亂之始，各有萌象。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that at the beginning of order and disorder, each has its budding signs.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard that at the beginning of order and disorder, each has its budding signs.

sentences.zh: 容直言，廣視聽，躬勤庶務，委信大臣，使左右近習不得蔽疏遠之人，此治象也。

translations.literal: Accepting blunt speech, broadening vision and hearing, personally attending to common affairs, entrusting and trusting great ministers, and keeping close favorites from blocking distant persons—this is the sign of order.
translations.idiomatic: Accepting blunt speech, broadening vision and hearing, personally attending to common affairs, entrusting and trusting great ministers, and keeping close favorites from blocking distant persons—this is the sign of order.

sentences.zh: 大臣不親，直言不進，抵忌諱者殺，犯左右者刑，與一二近習決事深宮中，群臣莫得與，此亂萌也。

translations.literal: Great ministers kept at a distance, blunt speech not admitted, those who touch taboos killed and those who offend favorites punished, deciding affairs with one or two close favorites deep in the palace while the ministers may not participate—this is the budding of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers kept at a distance, blunt speech not admitted, those who touch taboos killed and those who offend favorites punished, deciding affairs with one or two close favorites deep in the palace while the ministers may not participate—this is the budding of disorder.

sentences.zh: 人君始即位，萌象未見，必有狂直敢言者。

translations.literal: When a ruler first ascends the throne, before the budding signs appear, there are sure to be wild, blunt, outspoken men.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler first ascends the throne, before the budding signs appear, there are sure to be wild, blunt, outspoken men.

sentences.zh: 上或激而進之，則天下君子望風曰：「彼狂而容於上，其欲來天下士乎？

translations.literal: If the ruler sometimes provokes and promotes them, then the gentlemen of all under heaven look to the wind and say: "That wild man is tolerated by the ruler—is he seeking to summon the gentlemen of the realm?
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler sometimes provokes and promotes them, then the gentlemen of all under heaven look to the wind and say: "That wild man is tolerated by the ruler—is he seeking to summon the gentlemen of the realm?

sentences.zh: 吾之道可以行矣！」

translations.literal: My Way can be put into practice!"
translations.idiomatic: My Way can be put into practice!"

sentences.zh: 其小人則竦利曰：「彼之直，得幸於上，吾將直言以徼利乎！」

translations.literal: The petty men then, alert to profit, said: "That man's bluntness won favor from the ruler—I shall speak bluntly to seek profit!"
translations.idiomatic: The petty men then, scenting advantage, said: "That man's bluntness won favor from the ruler—shall I speak bluntly to seek profit for myself?"

sentences.zh: 由是天下賢不肖各以所忠貢於上，上下之志，霈然而通。

translations.literal: Thereupon the worthy and unworthy throughout the realm each offered what they held loyal to the ruler, and the intentions above and below flowed together like a great rain.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the worthy and unworthy throughout the realm each offered what they held loyal to the ruler, and the intentions above and below flowed together like a great rain.

sentences.zh: 合天下之智，治萬物之心，人人樂得其所，戴其上如赤子之親慈母也，雖欲誘之為亂，可得乎？

translations.literal: Combining the wisdom of all under heaven and governing the hearts of all things, every man gladly found his place and revered his ruler as an infant cherishes its loving mother—even if one wished to incite them to rebellion, could one succeed?
translations.idiomatic: Combining the wisdom of all under heaven and governing the hearts of all things, every man gladly found his place and revered his ruler as an infant cherishes its loving mother—even if one wished to incite them to rebellion, could one succeed?

sentences.zh: 及夫進計者入，而直言者戮，則天下君子內謀曰：「與其言不用而身為戮，吾甯危行言遜以保其終乎！」

translations.literal: When those who offered schemes were admitted while blunt speakers were executed, then the gentlemen of all under heaven plotted inwardly, saying: "Rather than speak and not be heeded while one's person is executed, had I not better practice perilous conduct with modest words to preserve my end!"
translations.idiomatic: When those who offered schemes were admitted while blunt speakers were executed, then the gentlemen of all under heaven plotted inwardly, saying: "Rather than speak and not be heeded while one's person is executed, had I not better practice perilous conduct with modest words to preserve my end!"

sentences.zh: 其小人則擇利曰：「吾君所惡者拂心逆耳，吾將苟順是非以事之。」

translations.literal: The petty men then chose profit, saying: "What our ruler hates is what goes against his heart and offends his ears—I shall casually follow right and wrong to serve him."
translations.idiomatic: The petty men then chose profit, saying: "What our ruler hates is what goes against his heart and offends his ears—I shall casually follow right and wrong to serve him."

sentences.zh: 由是進見者革而不內，言事者寢而不聞，若此則十步之事不得見，況天下四方之遠乎！

translations.literal: Thereupon those who came to audience were turned away and not admitted, and those who spoke on affairs were ignored and not heard; if matters ten paces away cannot be seen, how much less the distant reaches of all under heaven in the four directions!
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon those who came to audience were turned away and not admitted, and those who spoke on affairs were ignored and not heard; if matters ten paces away cannot be seen, how much less the distant reaches of all under heaven in the four directions!

sentences.zh: 故曰：聾瞽之君非無耳目，左右前後者遮罩之，不使視聽，欲不亂，可得哉？

translations.literal: Hence it is said: a deaf and blind ruler is not without eyes and ears—it is those at his left and right, before and behind, who screen and cover them, not letting him see or hear; if he wishes not to fall into disorder, can he succeed?
translations.idiomatic: Hence it is said: a deaf and blind ruler is not without eyes and ears—it is those at his left and right, before and behind, who screen and cover them, not letting him see or hear; if he wishes not to fall into disorder, can he succeed?

sentences.zh: 太宗初即位，天下莫有言者，孫伏伽以小事持諫，厚賜以勉之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong first ascended the throne, no one in all under heaven spoke up; Sun Fugai remonstrated over a small matter, and the Emperor richly rewarded him to encourage such conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong first ascended the throne, no one in all under heaven spoke up; Sun Fugai remonstrated over a small matter, and the Emperor richly rewarded him to encourage such conduct.

sentences.zh: 自是論事者唯懼言不直、諫不極、不能激上之盛意，曾不以忌諱為虞。

translations.literal: From then on those who discussed affairs feared only that their words were not blunt enough, their remonstrance not extreme enough, that they could not stir the ruler's full intent—they never took taboo as a concern.
translations.idiomatic: From then on those who discussed affairs feared only that their words were not blunt enough, their remonstrance not extreme enough, that they could not stir the ruler's full intent—they never took taboo as a concern.

sentences.zh: 於是房、杜、王、魏議可否於前，四方言得失於外，不數年大治。

translations.literal: Thereupon Fang, Du, Wang, and Wei debated what was feasible and what was not before the throne, and the four directions spoke of gains and losses from without; in a few years there was great order.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Fang, Du, Wang, and Wei debated what was feasible and what was not before the throne, and the four directions spoke of gains and losses from without; in a few years there was great order.

sentences.zh: 豈文皇獨運聰明於上哉？

translations.literal: Was it that Emperor Wen alone exercised wisdom above?
translations.idiomatic: Was it that Emperor Wen alone exercised wisdom above?

sentences.zh: 蓋下盡其言，以宣揚發暢之也。

translations.literal: It was because those below fully spoke their minds, and he spread and gave free course to it.
translations.idiomatic: It was because those below fully spoke their minds, and he spread and gave free course to their words.

sentences.zh: 夫樂全安，惡戮辱，古今情一也，豈獨貞觀之人輕犯忌諱而好戮辱哉？

translations.literal: To delight in preservation and safety and to hate execution and disgrace—the sentiment is one in ancient and modern times; were the people of the Zhenguan era alone light in violating taboos and fond of execution and disgrace?
translations.idiomatic: To delight in preservation and safety and to hate execution and disgrace—the sentiment is one in ancient and modern times; were the people of the Zhenguan era alone light in violating taboos and fond of execution and disgrace?

sentences.zh: 蓋上激而進之也。

translations.literal: It was because the ruler provoked and promoted them.
translations.idiomatic: It was because the ruler provoked and promoted them.

sentences.zh: 喜順從，怒謇犯，亦古今情一也，豈獨文皇甘逆耳、怒從心哉？

translations.literal: To delight in compliance and grow angry at blunt offense—the sentiment is likewise one in ancient and modern times; was Emperor Wen alone willing to accept what went against his ears and angry at what accorded with his heart?
translations.idiomatic: To delight in compliance and grow angry at blunt offense—the sentiment is likewise one in ancient and modern times; was Emperor Wen alone willing to accept what went against his ears and angry at what accorded with his heart?

sentences.zh: 蓋以順從之利輕，而危亡之禍大，思為子孫建永安計也。

translations.literal: It was because the profit of compliance was slight while the calamity of peril and ruin was great—he thought to establish a plan of lasting peace for his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: It was because the profit of compliance was slight while the calamity of peril and ruin was great—he thought to establish a plan of lasting peace for his descendants.

sentences.zh: 為後嗣者，其可順一朝意，而蔑文皇之天下乎？

translations.literal: For one who is a successor, can one comply with the whim of a single court and scorn the realm that Emperor Wen established?
translations.idiomatic: For one who is a successor, can one comply with the whim of a single court and scorn the realm that Emperor Wen established?

sentences.zh: 陛下即位已一歲，百辟卿士、天下四方之人，曾未有獻一計進一言而受賞者；

translations.literal: Your Majesty has been on the throne for a year, yet among the hundred officials and ministers and the people of all under heaven in the four directions, there has never been one who offered a plan or advanced a word and received reward;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has been on the throne for a year, yet among the hundred officials and ministers and the people of all under heaven in the four directions, there has never been one who offered a plan or advanced a word and received reward;

sentences.zh: 左右前後拾遺補闕，亦未有奏封執諫而蒙勸者。

translations.literal: Among the remonstrance officers at left and right, before and behind, there has likewise been none who submitted sealed memorials or held fast in remonstrance and received encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Among the remonstrance officers at left and right, before and behind, there has likewise been none who submitted sealed memorials or held fast in remonstrance and received encouragement.

sentences.zh: 設諫鼓，置匭函，曾未聞雪冤決事、明察幽之意者。

translations.literal: Though remonstrance drums were set up and suggestion boxes placed, there has never been heard the intent to redress wrongs, decide cases, and clearly examine what is hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Though remonstrance drums were set up and suggestion boxes placed, there has never been heard the intent to redress wrongs, decide cases, and clearly examine what is hidden.

sentences.zh: 以陛下睿博洪深，勵精求治，豈言而不用哉？

translations.literal: Given Your Majesty's wisdom, breadth, and profundity, and your striving spirit in seeking good government, could it be that words are spoken but not used?
translations.idiomatic: Given Your Majesty's wisdom, breadth, and profundity, and your striving spirit in seeking good government, could it be that words are spoken but not used?

sentences.zh: 蓋下不能有所發明耳！

translations.literal: It is simply that those below cannot bring forth anything illuminating!
translations.idiomatic: It is simply that those below cannot bring forth anything illuminating!

sentences.zh: 承顧問者，獨一二執政，對不及頃而罷，豈暇陳治安、議教化哉？

translations.literal: Those who received consultation were only one or two chief ministers; the audience lasted less than a moment and ended—how could there be leisure to set forth peace and order or discuss teaching and transformation?
translations.idiomatic: Those who received consultation were only one or two chief ministers; the audience lasted less than a moment and ended—how could there be leisure to set forth peace and order or discuss teaching and transformation?

sentences.zh: 它有司或時召見，僅能奉簿書計錢穀登降耳。

translations.literal: Other offices were sometimes summoned, but could only present ledgers and reckon the rise and fall of revenue and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Other offices were sometimes summoned, but could only present ledgers and reckon the rise and fall of revenue and grain.

sentences.zh: 以陛下之政，視貞觀何如哉？

translations.literal: Compared with the Zhenguan era, how does Your Majesty's governance stand?
translations.idiomatic: Compared with the Zhenguan era, how does Your Majesty's governance stand?

sentences.zh: 貞觀時，尚有房、杜、王、魏輔翊之智，日有獻可替否者。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era there were still the assisting wisdom of Fang, Du, Wang, and Wei, and daily there were those who offered what could be approved or rejected.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era there were still the assisting wisdom of Fang, Du, Wang, and Wei, and daily there were those who offered what could be approved or rejected.

sentences.zh: 今陛下當致治之初，而言事進計者歲無一人，豈非群下因循竊位之罪乎？

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty is at the beginning of bringing order, yet not one person in a year offers plans or speaks on affairs—is this not the fault of the officials below, who follow old ways and hold their posts by theft?
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty is at the beginning of bringing order, yet not one person in a year offers plans or speaks on affairs—is this not the fault of the officials below, who follow old ways and hold their posts by theft?

sentences.zh: 輒昧死條上十事：一、教太子，正邦本；

translations.literal: Your subject therefore dares set forth ten items at the risk of death: first, teach the crown prince and rectify the foundation of the state;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject therefore dares set forth ten items at the risk of death: first, teach the crown prince and rectify the foundation of the state;

sentences.zh: 二、封諸王，固磐石；

translations.literal: second, enfeoff the princes and solidify the bedrock;
translations.idiomatic: second, enfeoff the princes and solidify the bedrock;

sentences.zh: 三、出宮人；

translations.literal: third, release palace women;
translations.idiomatic: third, release palace women;

sentences.zh: 四、嫁宗女；

translations.literal: fourth, marry off imperial clanswomen;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, marry off imperial clanswomen;

sentences.zh: 五、時召宰相講庶政；

translations.literal: fifth, regularly summon the chancellors to discuss common affairs;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, regularly summon the chancellors to discuss common affairs;

sentences.zh: 六、次對群臣，廣聰明；

translations.literal: sixth, receive the ministers in sequence and broaden intelligence;
translations.idiomatic: sixth, receive the ministers in sequence and broaden intelligence;

sentences.zh: 七、復正衙奏事；

translations.literal: seventh, restore memorializing at the main court;
translations.idiomatic: seventh, restore memorializing at the main court;

sentences.zh: 八、許方幅糾彈；

translations.literal: eighth, permit impeachment within proper bounds;
translations.idiomatic: eighth, permit impeachment within proper bounds;

sentences.zh: 九、禁非時貢獻；

translations.literal: ninth, forbid untimely tribute offerings;
translations.idiomatic: ninth, forbid untimely tribute offerings;

sentences.zh: 十、省出入遊畋。

translations.literal: tenth, reduce going out and hunting excursions.
translations.idiomatic: tenth, reduce going out and hunting excursions.

sentences.zh: 于時論傪、高弘本、豆盧靖等出為刺史，閱旬，追還詔書。

translations.literal: At the time Lun Can, Gao Hongben, Dou Lu Jing, and others were sent out as prefects; within ten days edicts were issued recalling them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Lun Can, Gao Hongben, Dou Lu Jing, and others were sent out as prefects; within ten days edicts were issued recalling them.

sentences.zh: 稹諫：「詔令數易，不能信天下。」

translations.literal: Zhen remonstrated: "Edicts are changed repeatedly and cannot inspire trust throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen remonstrated: "Edicts are changed repeatedly and cannot inspire trust throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 又陳西北邊事。

translations.literal: He also set forth matters on the northwestern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He also set forth matters on the northwestern frontier.

sentences.zh: 憲宗悅，召問得失。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong was pleased and summoned him to ask about gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong was pleased and summoned him to ask about gains and losses.

sentences.zh: 當路者惡之，出為河南尉，以母喪解。

translations.literal: Those in power hated him and sent him out as Assistant Magistrate of Henan; he resigned on account of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power hated him and sent him out as Assistant Magistrate of Henan; he resigned on account of his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 服除，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 按獄東川，因劾奏節度使嚴礪違詔過賦數百萬，沒入塗山甫等八十余家田產奴婢。

translations.literal: Investigating cases in Dongchuan, he memorialized impeaching Military Governor Yan Li for exceeding the edict in taxation by several million, confiscating the fields, property, and slaves of more than eighty households including Tu Shanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating cases in Dongchuan, he memorialized impeaching Military Governor Yan Li for exceeding the edict in taxation by several million, confiscating the fields, property, and slaves of more than eighty households including Tu Shanfu.

sentences.zh: 時礪已死，七刺史皆奪俸，礪黨怒。

translations.literal: By then Li was already dead; seven prefects all had their salaries forfeited, and Li's faction grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: By then Li was already dead; seven prefects all had their salaries forfeited, and Li's faction grew angry.

sentences.zh: 俄分司東都。

translations.literal: Before long he was assigned to the Eastern Capital branch office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was assigned to the Eastern Capital branch office.

sentences.zh: 時浙西觀察使韓皋杖安吉令孫澥，數日死；

translations.literal: At the time Zhexi Observation Commissioner Han Gao beat Anji Magistrate Sun Xie, who died within days;
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhexi Observation Commissioner Han Gao beat Anji Magistrate Sun Xie, who died within days;

sentences.zh: 武甯王紹護送監軍孟升喪乘驛，內喪郵中，吏不敢止；

translations.literal: Prince of Wuning Shao escorted the funeral of Army Supervisor Meng Sheng by post relay; the inner mourning passed through the postal stations and officials dared not stop it;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wuning Shao escorted the funeral of Army Supervisor Meng Sheng by post relay; the inner mourning passed through the postal stations and officials dared not stop it;

sentences.zh: 內園擅系人逾年，台不及知；

translations.literal: the Inner Park arbitrarily detained people for more than a year, and the Censorate did not learn of it in time;
translations.idiomatic: the Inner Park arbitrarily detained people for more than a year, and the Censorate did not learn of it in time;

sentences.zh: 河南尹誣殺諸生尹太階；

translations.literal: the Henan Intendant falsely killed the student Yin Taijie;
translations.idiomatic: the Henan Intendant falsely killed the student Yin Taijie;

sentences.zh: 飛龍使誘亡命奴為養子；

translations.literal: the Flying Dragon Commissioner enticed fugitive slaves to become adopted sons;
translations.idiomatic: the Flying Dragon Commissioner enticed fugitive slaves to become adopted sons;

sentences.zh: 田季安盜取洛陽衣冠女；

translations.literal: Tian Ji'an stole away a genteel woman of Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: Tian Ji'an stole away a genteel woman of Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 汴州沒入死賈錢千萬。

translations.literal: Bianzhou confiscated ten million in dead merchants' money.
translations.idiomatic: Bianzhou confiscated ten million in dead merchants' money.

sentences.zh: 凡十餘事，悉論奏。

translations.literal: More than ten such matters in all were fully memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten such matters in all were fully memorialized.

sentences.zh: 會河南尹房式坐罪，稹舉劾，按故事追攝，移書停務。

translations.literal: When Henan Intendant Fang Shi was implicated in a crime, Zhen memorialized impeachment; following precedent he was summoned for arrest and a letter was sent suspending his duties.
translations.idiomatic: When Henan Intendant Fang Shi was implicated in a crime, Zhen memorialized impeachment; following precedent he was summoned for arrest and a letter was sent suspending his duties.

sentences.zh: 詔薄式罪，召稹還。

translations.literal: An edict lightened Shi's offense and summoned Zhen back.
translations.idiomatic: An edict lightened Shi's offense and summoned Zhen back.

sentences.zh: 次敷水驛，中人仇士良夜至，稹不讓，中人怒，擊稹敗面。

translations.literal: Stopping at Fushui Post, the eunuch Qiu Shiliang came at night; Zhen did not yield, the eunuch grew angry, and struck Zhen, disfiguring his face.
translations.idiomatic: Stopping at Fushui Post, the eunuch Qiu Shiliang came at night; Zhen did not yield, the eunuch grew angry, and struck Zhen, disfiguring his face.

sentences.zh: 宰相以稹年少輕樹威，失憲臣體，貶江陵士曹參軍，而李絳、崔群、白居易皆論其枉。

translations.literal: The chancellors held that Zhen, young in years, lightly sought to establish authority and failed the proper bearing of a censorial official; he was demoted to Army Staff Officer of Jiangling, while Li Jiang, Cui Qun, and Bai Juyi all argued that he had been wronged.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors held that Zhen, young in years, lightly sought to establish authority and failed the proper bearing of a censorial official; he was demoted to Army Staff Officer of Jiangling, while Li Jiang, Cui Qun, and Bai Juyi all argued that he had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 久乃徙通州司馬，改虢州長史。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Prefectural Militia Vice Commandant of Tongzhou and then changed to Senior Administrator of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was transferred to Prefectural Militia Vice Commandant of Tongzhou and then changed to Senior Administrator of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 元和末，召拜膳部員外郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanhe he was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Board of Provisions.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yuanhe he was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Board of Provisions.

sentences.zh: 稹尤長於詩，與居易名相埒，天下傳諷，號「元和體」，往往播樂府。

translations.literal: Zhen was especially skilled in poetry; his fame rivaled Juyi's, and their works were recited throughout the realm; they were called the "Yuanhe Style" and were often set to music in the Music Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was especially skilled in poetry; his fame rivaled Juyi's, and their works were recited throughout the realm; they were called the "Yuanhe Style" and were often set to music in the Music Bureau.

sentences.zh: 穆宗在東宮，妃嬪近習皆誦之，宮中呼元才子。

translations.literal: When Muzong was in the Eastern Palace, consorts and close attendants all recited them, and within the palace he was called Talent Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong was in the Eastern Palace, consorts and close attendants all recited them, and within the palace he was called Talent Yuan.

sentences.zh: 稹之謫江陵，善臨軍崔潭峻。

translations.literal: When Zhen was banished to Jiangling, he became close to Army Officer Cui Tanjun.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen was banished to Jiangling, he became close to Army Officer Cui Tanjun.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，潭駿方親幸，以稹歌詞數十百篇奏禦，帝大悅，問：「稹今安在？」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing, Tanjun was then in close favor; he presented several dozen or hundred of Zhen's song lyrics to the throne; the Emperor was greatly pleased and asked: "Where is Zhen now?"
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Changqing, Tanjun was then in close favor; he presented several dozen or hundred of Zhen's song lyrics to the throne; the Emperor was greatly pleased and asked: "Where is Zhen now?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「為南宮散郎。」

translations.literal: The reply was: "He serves as a scattered officer of the Southern Palace."
translations.idiomatic: The reply was: "He serves as a scattered officer of the Southern Palace."

sentences.zh: 即擢祠部郎中，知制誥。

translations.literal: He was immediately promoted to Director of the Board of Sacrifices and put in charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately promoted to Director of the Board of Sacrifices and put in charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 變詔書體，務純厚明切，盛傳一時。

translations.literal: He changed the style of edicts, striving for pure thickness, clarity, and directness, and for a time they were widely circulated.
translations.idiomatic: He changed the style of edicts, striving for pure thickness, clarity, and directness, and for a time they were widely circulated.

sentences.zh: 然其進非公議，為士類訾薄。

translations.literal: Yet his advancement was not by public consensus and was scorned by the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his advancement was not by public consensus and was scorned by the gentry.

sentences.zh: 稹內不平，因《誡風俗詔》曆詆群有司，以逞其憾。

translations.literal: Zhen was inwardly resentful and, through the "Edict Admonishing Social Customs," repeatedly denounced the various offices to vent his grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was inwardly resentful and, through the "Edict Admonishing Social Customs," repeatedly denounced the various offices to vent his grievance.

sentences.zh: 俄遷中書舍人、翰林承旨學士。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Drafting Secretary and Hanlin Academician in Charge.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Drafting Secretary and Hanlin Academician in Charge.

sentences.zh: 數召入，禮遇益厚，自謂得言天下事。

translations.literal: He was summoned repeatedly, his reception grew ever more generous, and he considered himself able to speak on affairs of all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned repeatedly, his reception grew ever more generous, and he considered himself able to speak on affairs of all under heaven.

sentences.zh: 中人爭與稹交，魏弘簡在樞密，尤相善。

translations.literal: Eunuchs vied to associate with Zhen; Wei Hongjian was in the Secretariat and was especially close to him.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs vied to associate with Zhen; Wei Hongjian was in the Secretariat and was especially close to him.

sentences.zh: 裴度出屯鎮州，有所論奏，共沮卻之。

translations.literal: When Pei Du went out to encamp at Zhenzhou and submitted memorials, they jointly obstructed and rejected them.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du went out to encamp at Zhenzhou and submitted memorials, they jointly obstructed and rejected them.

sentences.zh: 度三上疏劾弘簡、稹傾亂國政：「陛下欲平賊，當先清朝廷乃可。」

translations.literal: Du thrice submitted memorials impeaching Hongjian and Zhen for overturning state affairs: "If Your Majesty wishes to suppress the rebels, you must first clarify the court before it can be done."
translations.idiomatic: Du thrice submitted memorials impeaching Hongjian and Zhen for overturning state affairs: "If Your Majesty wishes to suppress the rebels, you must first clarify the court before it can be done."

sentences.zh: 帝迫群議，乃罷弘簡，而出稹為工部侍郎。

translations.literal: The Emperor, pressed by public opinion, then dismissed Hongjian and sent Zhen out as Vice Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, pressed by public opinion, then dismissed Hongjian and sent Zhen out as Vice Minister of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 然眷倚不衰。

translations.literal: Yet imperial favor did not wane.
translations.idiomatic: Yet imperial favor did not wane.

sentences.zh: 未幾，進同中書門下平章事，朝野雜然輕笑，稹思立奇節報天子以厭人心。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Director of the Chancellery; court and commoners alike laughed lightly at this, and Zhen thought to establish a singular deed to repay the Son of Heaven and satisfy popular sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Director of the Chancellery; court and commoners alike laughed lightly at this, and Zhen thought to establish a singular deed to repay the Son of Heaven and satisfy popular sentiment.

sentences.zh: 時王廷湊方圍牛元翼於深州，稹所善於方言：「王昭、于友明皆豪士，雅游燕、趙間，能得賊要領，可使反間而出元翼。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Tingcou was besieging Niu Yuanji at Shenzhou; a man Zhen favored named Fang Yan said: "Wang Zhao and Yu Youming are both bold men who freely traveled between Yan and Zhao; they can grasp the rebels' vital points and can be used in counter-intelligence to rescue Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Tingcou was besieging Niu Yuanji at Shenzhou; a man Zhen favored named Fang Yan said: "Wang Zhao and Yu Youming are both bold men who freely traveled between Yan and Zhao; they can grasp the rebels' vital points and can be used in counter-intelligence to rescue Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 願以家貲辦行，得兵部虛告二十，以便宜募士。」

translations.literal: I wish to use my family wealth to arrange the journey, obtain twenty blank commissions from the Ministry of War, and recruit men as expedient."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to use my family wealth to arrange the journey, obtain twenty blank commissions from the Ministry of War, and recruit men as expedient."

sentences.zh: 稹然之。

translations.literal: Zhen approved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen approved.

sentences.zh: 李逢吉知其謀，陰令李賞訹裴度曰：「于方為稹結客，將刺公。」

translations.literal: Li Fengji learned of the plan and secretly had Li Shang slander Pei Du, saying: "Yu Fang is gathering clients for Zhen and intends to assassinate you."
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengji learned of the plan and secretly had Li Shang slander Pei Du, saying: "Yu Fang is gathering clients for Zhen and intends to assassinate you."

sentences.zh: 度隱不發。

translations.literal: Du kept silent and did not expose it.
translations.idiomatic: Du kept silent and did not expose it.

sentences.zh: 神策軍中尉以聞，詔韓皋、鄭覃及逢吉雜治，無刺度狀，而方計暴聞，遂與度偕罷宰相，出為同州刺史。

translations.literal: The Army Supervising Eunuch of the Shence Armies reported it; an edict ordered Han Gao, Zheng Tan, and Fengji jointly to investigate; there was no evidence of a plot against Du, but Fang's plan was suddenly exposed, and Zhen was dismissed from the chancellorship together with Du and sent out as Prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Army Supervising Eunuch of the Shence Armies reported it; an edict ordered Han Gao, Zheng Tan, and Fengji jointly to investigate; there was no evidence of a plot against Du, but Fang's plan was suddenly exposed, and Zhen was dismissed from the chancellorship together with Du and sent out as Prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 諫官爭言度不當免，而黜稹輕。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials contended that Du should not have been dismissed while Zhen's demotion was too light.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials contended that Du should not have been dismissed while Zhen's demotion was too light.

sentences.zh: 帝獨憐稹，但削長春宮使。

translations.literal: The Emperor alone pitied Zhen and only removed him from the post of Changchun Palace Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor alone pitied Zhen and only removed him from the post of Changchun Palace Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 初，獄未具，京兆劉遵古遣吏羅禁稹第，稹訴之，帝怒，責京兆，免捕賊尉，使使者慰稹。

translations.literal: Initially, before the case was complete, Jingzhao Intendant Liu Zungu sent officials to surround and seal Zhen's residence; Zhen complained, the Emperor grew angry, rebuked Jingzhao, dismissed the arresting captain, and sent an envoy to comfort Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, before the case was complete, Jingzhao Intendant Liu Zungu sent officials to surround and seal Zhen's residence; Zhen complained, the Emperor grew angry, rebuked Jingzhao, dismissed the arresting captain, and sent an envoy to comfort Zhen.

sentences.zh: 再期，徙浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: At the next term he was transferred to Zhedong Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the next term he was transferred to Zhedong Observation Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明州歲貢蚶，役郵子萬人，不勝其疲，稹奏罷之。

translations.literal: Mingzhou annually tribute-offered clams, conscripting ten thousand postal workers who could not bear the exhaustion; Zhen memorialized to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhou annually tribute-offered clams, conscripting ten thousand postal workers who could not bear the exhaustion; Zhen memorialized to abolish it.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，召為尚書左丞，務振綱紀，出郎官尤無狀者七人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe he was summoned as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, striving to restore discipline and removing seven bureau directors who were especially unfit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taihe he was summoned as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, striving to restore discipline and removing seven bureau directors who were especially unfit.

sentences.zh: 然稹素無檢，望輕，不為公議所右。

translations.literal: Yet Zhen had long been unrestrained, his prestige was slight, and public opinion did not favor him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhen had long been unrestrained, his prestige was slight, and public opinion did not favor him.

sentences.zh: 王播卒，謀復輔政甚力，訖不遂。

translations.literal: When Wang Bo died, he plotted vigorously to return to auxiliary governance but ultimately did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Bo died, he plotted vigorously to return to auxiliary governance but ultimately did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 俄拜武昌節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed military governor of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed military governor of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十三，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty-three and was posthumously enfeoffed as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-three and was posthumously enfeoffed as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 所論著甚多，行於世。

translations.literal: His writings were numerous and circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His writings were numerous and circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 在越時，辟竇鞏。

translations.literal: While in Yue he recruited Dou Gong.
translations.idiomatic: While in Yue he recruited Dou Gong.

sentences.zh: 鞏，天下工為詩，與之酬和，故鏡湖秦望之奇益傳，時號「蘭亭絕唱」。

translations.literal: Gong was skilled in poetry throughout the realm; they exchanged verses, and thus the wonders of Mirror Lake and Mount Qinwang spread still further; at the time they were called the "Supreme Song of Lanting."
translations.idiomatic: Gong was skilled in poetry throughout the realm; they exchanged verses, and thus the wonders of Mirror Lake and Mount Qinwang spread still further; at the time they were called the "Supreme Song of Lanting."

sentences.zh: 稹始言事峭直，欲以立名，中見斥廢十年，通道不堅，乃喪所守。

translations.literal: Zhen at first spoke bluntly on affairs, wishing to establish a name; midway he was dismissed and cast aside for ten years; his grasp of the Way was not firm, and he lost what he had held to.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen at first spoke bluntly on affairs, wishing to establish a name; midway he was dismissed and cast aside for ten years; his grasp of the Way was not firm, and he lost what he had held to.

sentences.zh: 附宦貴得宰相，居位才三月罷。

translations.literal: Attaching himself to eunuch nobles he obtained the chancellorship, but held office only three months before dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Attaching himself to eunuch nobles he obtained the chancellorship, but held office only three months before dismissal.

sentences.zh: 晚節彌沮喪，加廉節不飾雲。

translations.literal: His late years grew ever more dejected, and moreover he no longer cultivated integrity and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: His late years grew ever more dejected, and moreover he no longer cultivated integrity and restraint.

sentences.zh: 牛僧儒牛僧孺，字思黯，隋僕射奇章公弘之裔。

translations.literal: Niu Sengru—Niu Sengru, styled Si'an, was a descendant of Sui Vice Director Lord Qizhang Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Sengru, styled Si'an, was a descendant of Sui Vice Director Lord Qizhang Hong.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，下杜樊鄉有賜田數頃，依以為生。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he had several qing of granted fields at Xiadufan Village and relied on them for a living.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned while young, he had several qing of granted fields at Xiadufan Village and relied on them for a living.

sentences.zh: 工屬文，第進士。

translations.literal: He was skilled at composition and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at composition and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 元和初，以賢良方正對策，與李宗閔、皇甫湜俱第一，條指失政，其言鯁訐，不避宰相。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, in the Exemplary and Upright policy response he ranked first together with Li Zongmin and Huangfu Shi; he listed failures of governance, his words blunt and accusatory, not avoiding the chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanhe, in the Exemplary and Upright policy response he ranked first together with Li Zongmin and Huangfu Shi; he listed failures of governance, his words blunt and accusatory, not avoiding the chancellors.

sentences.zh: 宰相怒，故楊于陵、鄭敬、韋貫之、李益等坐考非其宜，皆調去。

translations.literal: The chancellors grew angry, and therefore Yang Yuling, Zheng Jing, Wei Guanzhi, Li Yi, and others were all demoted for improper evaluation and transferred away.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors grew angry, and therefore Yang Yuling, Zheng Jing, Wei Guanzhi, Li Yi, and others were all demoted for improper evaluation and transferred away.

sentences.zh: 僧孺調伊闕尉，改河南，遷監察御史，進累考工員外郎、集賢殿直學士。

translations.literal: Sengru was transferred to Assistant Magistrate of Yique, changed to Henan, promoted to Investigating Censor, and advanced through accumulated appointments to Vice Director of the Board of Works and Direct Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Sengru was transferred to Assistant Magistrate of Yique, changed to Henan, promoted to Investigating Censor, and advanced through accumulated appointments to Vice Director of the Board of Works and Direct Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 穆宗初，以庫部郎中知制誥。

translations.literal: When Muzong first took the throne, he was made Director of the Board of the Treasury and put in charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong first took the throne, he was made Director of the Board of the Treasury and put in charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 徙御史中丞，按治不法，內外澄肅。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Investigation Commissioner and investigated lawlessness; within and without the court grew clear and disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Investigation Commissioner and investigated lawlessness; within and without the court grew clear and disciplined.

sentences.zh: 宿州刺史李直臣坐賕當死，賂宦侍為助，具獄上。

translations.literal: Suzhou Prefect Li Zhichen was implicated in bribery and deserved death; he bribed eunuch attendants for help, and the complete case was submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou Prefect Li Zhichen was implicated in bribery and deserved death; he bribed eunuch attendants for help, and the complete case was submitted.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「直臣有才，朕欲貸而用之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Zhichen has talent; I wish to pardon him and employ him."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Zhichen has talent; I wish to pardon him and employ him.

sentences.zh: 僧孺曰：「彼不才者，持祿取容耳。

translations.literal: Sengru said: "Those without talent merely hold salary and seek favor.
translations.idiomatic: Sengru said: "Those without talent merely hold salary and seek favor.

sentences.zh: 天子制法，所以束縛有才者。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven makes laws in order to bind those with talent.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven makes laws in order to bind those with talent.

sentences.zh: 祿山、硃泚以才過人，故亂天下。」

translations.literal: An Lushan and Zhu Ci exceeded others in talent and therefore threw the realm into disorder."
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan and Zhu Ci exceeded others in talent and therefore threw the realm into disorder.

sentences.zh: 帝異其言，乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor was struck by his words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was struck by his words and stopped.

sentences.zh: 賜金紫服，以戶部侍郎同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was granted gold and purple robes and made Vice Minister of Revenue and Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted gold and purple robes and made Vice Minister of Revenue and Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 始，韓弘入朝，其子公武用財賂權貴，杜塞言者。

translations.literal: Initially, when Han Hong came to court, his son Gongwu used wealth to bribe the powerful and block those who spoke.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when Han Hong came to court, his son Gongwu used wealth to bribe the powerful and block those who spoke.

sentences.zh: 俄而弘、公武卒，孫弱不能事，帝遣使者至其家，悉收貲簿，校計出入。

translations.literal: Before long Hong and Gongwu died; the grandson was weak and could not manage affairs; the Emperor sent envoys to their house and collected all account books, checking income and outgo.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Hong and Gongwu died; the grandson was weak and could not manage affairs; the Emperor sent envoys to their house and collected all account books, checking income and outgo.

sentences.zh: 所以餉中朝臣者皆在，至僧孺，獨注其左曰：「某月日，送錢千萬，不納。」

translations.literal: Those who had been fed to court ministers were all recorded; for Sengru alone a note was made on the left: "On such-and-such month and day, ten million in cash was sent and not accepted."
translations.idiomatic: Those who had been fed to court ministers were all recorded; for Sengru alone a note was made on the left: "On such-and-such month and day, ten million in cash was sent and not accepted.

sentences.zh: 帝善之，謂左右曰：「吾不謬知人。」

translations.literal: The Emperor approved and said to those around him: "I do not misjudge men."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved and said to those around him: "I do not misjudge men.

sentences.zh: 繇是遂以相。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was made chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was made chancellor.

sentences.zh: 尋遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 敬宗立，進封奇章郡公。

translations.literal: When Jingzong took the throne, he was advanced and enfeoffed as Duke of Qizhang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzong took the throne, he was advanced and enfeoffed as Duke of Qizhang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 是時政出近幸，僧孺數表去位，帝為于鄂州置武昌軍，授武昌節度使、同平章事。

translations.literal: At the time government came from close favorites; Sengru repeatedly memorialized to leave office, and the Emperor established the Wuchang Army at Ezhou for him, appointing him military governor of Wuchang and Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: At the time government came from close favorites; Sengru repeatedly memorialized to leave office, and the Emperor established the Wuchang Army at Ezhou for him, appointing him military governor of Wuchang and Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 鄂城土惡亟圮，歲增築，賦蓑茅於民，吏倚為擾。

translations.literal: The soil of Ezhou city was poor and the walls constantly collapsed; each year they were rebuilt and thatch was levied on the people, and officials relied on this as a source of harassment.
translations.idiomatic: The soil of Ezhou city was poor and the walls constantly collapsed; each year they were rebuilt and thatch was levied on the people, and officials relied on this as a source of harassment.

sentences.zh: 僧孺陶甓以城，五年畢，鄂人無復歲費。

translations.literal: Sengru fired bricks to build the walls; in five years it was complete, and the people of E no longer had annual expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Sengru fired bricks to build the walls; in five years it was complete, and the people of E no longer had annual expenses.

sentences.zh: 又廢沔州以省冗官。

translations.literal: He also abolished Mianzhou to reduce redundant officials.
translations.idiomatic: He also abolished Mianzhou to reduce redundant officials.

sentences.zh: 文宗立，李宗閔當國，屢稱僧孺賢，不宜棄外。

translations.literal: When Wenzong took the throne, Li Zongmin held power and repeatedly praised Sengru as worthy and unfit to be cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong took the throne, Li Zongmin held power and repeatedly praised Sengru as worthy and unfit to be cast aside.

sentences.zh: 復以兵部尚書平章事。

translations.literal: He was again made Minister of War and Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Minister of War and Director of the Chancellery.
